title: Telemetry-guided priority lanes for air-gapped / private onboarding
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Summary: Define and implement a telemetry-driven intake and prioritization system for Private/VPC/on-prem customer requests that are constrained by network topology, upgrades, or air-gapped environments. The goal is to reduce time-to-onboard for low-friction customers (fast-lane) while surfacing high-risk installs into a structured remediation path (staged-lane).

Why: Current intake relies heavily on manual triage and ad-hoc probing from SEs; we see repeated delays caused by missing network telemetry, unclear upgrade compatibility, and unknown proxy/firewall behaviors. A telemetry-first rubric will give us objective signals for routing requests to (1) self-serve fast-path, (2) SE-assisted staged rollout, or (3) engineering remediation backlog.

Scope:
- Intake enhancements (form + automated probe or customer-run probe collector)
- Scoring rubric using network telemetry (eg. egress IPs allowed, TLS interception detected, DNS resolution latency, NAT/port mappings, corporate proxy presence)
- Priority lanes: Fast-path (self-serve + docs), Staged (concierge onboarding), Blocked/Engineering (requires infra changes or custom proxy bridge)
- Dashboards in Console for in-flight onboards and ML model to predict time-to-ready based on signals
- Handoff document and runbook templates for Solutions Engineering and Customer Success

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form captures required fields + optional probe bundle link
- Automated scoring produces a 0-100 compatibility score and recommended lane with reasoning text
- >= 30% of qualifying requests are placed into Fast-path in first month of launch (target: 30–50%)
- Dashboards show per-customer signal breakdown and average time-to-ready per lane
- Runbooks exist and SEs trained; first pilot with two paying customers completed

Non-goals: Full auto-remediation of networking issues (we will provide remediation guidance and a proxy pattern, not a one-click fix).

Artifacts: Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONBOARD/Telemetry+Priority+Lanes
Design mockups: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b-onboarding-lanes
comments: 2026-03-02 Marcus Nguyen: Initial proposal drafted after interviews with 7 SEs and 4 pilot customers; most friction points are missing egress rules and corporate proxies that rewrite TLS.
2026-03-04 Aisha Patel: Added scoring dimensions and proposed thresholds. Suggest adding an optional customer-run probe tool to avoid collecting credentials.
2026-03-07 Engineering review (K. Morales): Runtime can accept probe metadata via signed JSON blob; must validate schema and strip PII before persisting.
2026-03-09 Security (L. Chen): Approved probe approach if telemetry is opt-in and stored encrypted in customer-scoped namespace; KMS integration required.
2026-03-11 SE feedback (R. Alvarez): Fast-path docs need clearer firewall templates and a sample iptables+proxy bypass snippet; will collaborate on sample scripts.

2026-03-13 PM sync: Agreed pilot plan: two customers (one EU financial, one US SaaS) for staged lane; build dashboard sprinters for visibility; create success metrics dashboard: time-to-ready, percent fast-path.
2026-03-15 Aisha Patel: Updated ticket with acceptance criteria and dependencies; opened GH issue for probe schema (github.com/redwood-inference/onboard-probe/issues/12).
sample_scoring_rubric: Score components (weights): egress-open-ports (20), tls-intercept-detected (25), dns-resolution-stable (15), nat-behavior-known (10), proxy-present-but-passive (10), documented-admin-cooperation (20). Example: egress-open-ports=true (20) + tls-intercept=false (0) + dns-stable=10 + nat-known=10 + proxy-passive=10 + admin-coop=20 => total 70 => Staged lane recommended.
pilot_plan: Week 0: Instrument intake + probe collector. Week 1-2: Pilot with EU financial customer (staged). Week 3: Pilot with US SaaS (fast-path eligible). Week 4: Evaluate metrics, tweak thresholds, roll to 10% of new private requests.
notes: We should avoid storing raw packet captures. Probe collector will capture metadata and traceroutes; sensitive values will be hashed. Legal has requested a short consent artifact for customers in EU region.
